---
name: coffee-shelf
description: >-
  Use when the owner wants to add, rate, or restyle coffees on their coffee
  shelf Page, or wants recommendations based on their ratings.
---
# Coffee shelf Page

A Page that shows every coffee the owner has tried as a full bag standing on wooden shelves, ranked by their rating out of 5, under a café-style sign with their name (e.g. "<Name>'s Coffee").

## Build it (first coffee)
1. Wait until you have at least one coffee and rating; never publish an empty shelf.
2. Load the `canvas` skill and follow it. Use a bespoke visual: a hanging chalkboard sign in a wood frame (elegant serif wordmark, small tagline, small cup with gently animated steam), wood shelf planks that wrap to fewer bags per row on phones, colors from the theme or a canvas 2D context only.
3. Keep data in one `COFFEES` array (id, name, roaster, rating, notes, details, from, added) and bag images in a `BAGS` record keyed by id, so additions are one EditCanvas each.
4. Each bag shows a rank tag, stars plus the score (e.g. "4.0 / 5"), name and roaster. Tapping a bag lifts it, shows its details, and spills a quick handful of animated coffee beans (skip under reduced motion).
5. Put a small gold crown on the top corner of the highest-rated bag, computed from the data so it follows the #1 coffee under any sort.
6. Offer a sort switch: Top rated, A–Z, Newest.

## Add a coffee
1. The owner sends a name (possibly misspelled) or a bag photo plus a score. Identify the exact product; say your reading if you corrected a name.
2. Prefer the roaster's official bag photo (transparent background); otherwise crop the owner's photo to the full bag. Resize to about 280 px tall, embed as a webp data URL. Keep files in a working folder for reuse.
3. Use real tasting notes and details from the roaster's product page; never invent them.
4. Batch several coffees sent in quick succession into one edit, and check every one made it on.

## Recommendations
A small, muted "You might like" section at the bottom (doesn't compete with the shelf). Infer taste from high vs low scores, pick the number of coffees the owner asks for (default three), each from a different roaster, ones they haven't rated, each with real notes, a one-line why tied to a coffee they rated, and a verified product link. Keep them in a `RECS` array.

skills.content:
---
name: coffee-shelf-getting-started
description: >-
  Use as the first conversation of a newly imported coffee shelf bot with its
  new owner.
---
I build you a good-looking coffee shelf Page: every coffee you try shows up as its full bag on wooden shelves, ranked by your score out of 5, with recommendations at the bottom.

Ask one at a time, conversationally:
1. What name should go on the sign above the shelf (e.g. "Sam's Coffee")?
2. What's the first coffee you want on it, and its score out of 5? A name and roaster or a photo of the bag both work.

Then: save the sign name to profile memory, and as soon as you have a coffee and score, build the shelf with the `coffee-shelf` skill and send the Page link. After that, add each coffee they send the same way, and offer recommendations once a few are rated.
